EXCERPT FROM: Contemporary, Issue 33 — Spring Edition, 3870

Mydeimos Nikador, virtuoso-turned-rockstar: “How I learned to love

music again” [TRANSCRIPT]

Interviewer: After starting work on this new album, your performances have taken a stark turn from how they used to be perceived by the classical music community. Do you have anything particular to say about this?

Mydei: Um. Well, I think I’ve been very obsessed with making my music perfect for my whole life, really. I never understood the appeal of allowing the music to take control, because if I ever lost control, I feared it would lose its accuracy, and I thought that making perfect music was playing it exactly as written. It took a lot of work to lose that habit.

Interviewer: Was there any moment in particular where something changed in your perception?

Mydei: Oh, definitely. I could name the exact day.

Interviewer: Really?

Mydei: (nods) May fourth, 3865.

Interviewer: Wow. And what happened?

Mydei: (pause) Something just clicked. I guess. It was right before I walked on stage, actually, and now that particular performance of mine is one of the most cited interpretations of the piece.

Interviewer: What piece was it?

Mydei: Chopin’s étude no. 3 in E Major…very misunderstood piece, at least that’s what the classical music fanatics say. I wouldn’t know.

Interviewer: Would you say you understood it, then?

Mydei: (laughs) I guess.

Interviewer: Anything in particular that caused this understanding to come about?

Mydei: It definitely wasn’t always there. I hated that piece up until the moment I finished my performance and realized that I had just done something people were going to love. But obviously it wasn’t, like, hatred that was coming through during my performance, but rather, well. I don’t know. I guess it just clicked in my brain for the first time who I was playing for.

Interviewer: Someone specific?

Mydei: (pause) Yeah.

Interviewer: Did this realization change your approach long term, or was it just the one piece?

Mydei: That night was the first time I think I made real music. I’ve been trying to chase that feeling ever since.

Interviewer: Do you think you have?

Mydei: (nods) I love the music I’ve made in this album more than anything. Honestly [expletive] Chopin, that performance wasn’t even that good when I look back on it.

Interviewer: (laughs) When you’re performing today, do you still do it for that same person?

Mydei: (sighs) Yeah.

~~~

May 3rd, 3865. Freshman spring.

Mydei finishes the piece with a flourish. His hands lift off the keys, and his foot off the pedal so he doesn’t hold the last note out for longer than necessary.

He looks back at Madam Herta nervously. He certainly thinks he’s ready for the concert tomorrow night, but if he knows one thing for sure it’s that Madam Herta is always impossible to impress. All Mydei wants is for her to clap for him, to finally see that he’s talented, that he can do this. But that dream is seeming increasingly unlikely.

“Do you know who said the quote, ‘to play a wrong note is insignificant, but to play without passion is inexcusable’?”

Mydei wets his lips. He’d heard that quote a thousand times before—it’s the kind of thing he might have cared to listen to five years ago, but now it just goes in one ear and out the other. He names the first composer he can think of. “Beethoven?”

“Wrong. Me.”

Mydei grimaces.

“Why do you think I am mentioning this quote, Mydeimos?”

“Because I played the notes right, but played without passion.”

“And you are going to improve this by tomorrow night.”

Mydei nods. He means it. He always focuses too much on the notes, playing exactly what’s written, and in this haze forgets that he’s supposed to be making music.

Madam Herta uncrosses her legs, and rests her glasses on the top of her head. “Well then. I suppose playing the notes perfectly is something to be proud of.”

She doesn’t mean it as a compliment. Mydei doesn’t take it as one.

He leaves her office after that, their lesson time over, and isn’t sure what to think. Madam Herta hadn’t been mean to him, but he’d heard from her older students that she was only ever mean to her students when they let her down. He’s faced with the undeniable fact that he hadn’t let her down, but only because she didn’t particularly believe in him in the first place.

He sits at the piano bench in one of the only empty practice rooms at this hour, but isn’t sure where to start. He can play the piece over and over again, but he won’t be able to tell if his playing is up to Madam Herta’s standards unless she’s right in front of him.

After an hour of workshopping, playing random passages over and over and trying to emulate the phrasing of random performance videos he found online, he settles on his last resort and calls Phainon.

Mydei has to wait four rings before he picks up, which is unusual.

“Mydei?” His voice is a little bit muffled, and a little rough, like he hadn’t spoken for a bit. “Is everything okay?”

“Yes,” Mydei says. “I’m okay. Did I wake you?” Phainon, asleep before ten PM is a foreign concept to Mydei. Sometimes, he thinks the man must be an insomniac or something.

“No, not at all, I…I wasn’t asleep.” Mydei can vaguely hear the sound of someone else laughing in the background, before Phainon shushes him.

“Shut it, Caelus, you’ll understand when you—” the rest of his sentence is cut off by a loud sound as Phainon presumably covers the microphone. “What is it, Mydei?” he asks afterwards, voice clearer now.

“Can I ask you a question?”

“Of course you can. Are you sure you’re okay?”

Mydei ignores the last part. “Phainon, when you’re playing…” he starts, thinking for a moment before continuing. “How do you do it? How are you able to immerse yourself so well?” Mydei has seen Phainon perform several times, and he’s seen him practice many more times. Each time, it’s like he loses himself in the music entirely. Like he opens his eyes when he’s done and has forgotten where he even was. It’s the one thing Mydei can’t do.

“Well…I don’t really know, Mydei,” he starts. “I don’t exactly do it by choice, I guess. I just love the music so much, and I love performing. I guess it kind of just happens.”

Mydei hums in response, not sure what else to say to that.

“Which étude are you playing again?” Phainon asks, in response to Mydei’s silence.

“E major,” Mydei responds. The music school decided to give each of the piano performance majors a Chopin étude to perform this semester, so that there was a cohesive theme to the concert and no one performance dragged out for too long. There were twenty-seven Madam Herta had to choose from, and there were about twenty Mydei would have preferred. It took him three weeks to realize she wasn’t playing an elaborate prank on him.

“Oh.”

“Oh.”

“Yeah. Not your style.”

“No.”

If only Professor Anaxa and Madam Herta switched their assignments around. Phainon was given a fast piece Mydei could have mastered in two weeks, tops. Mydei was given one of the slowest, most emotional pieces, out of all their options.

“Herta wasn’t happy?”

“No.” Mydei bites his tongue, suddenly getting annoyed all over again. “It’s hard to play it with any amount of passion when I don’t even like the piece.”

“You can’t find anything to like about it?”

“No. It sucks.”

“Well, sorry. It is what it is, Mydei.”

Mydei sighs, loudly, into his phone.

“Don’t sigh. You’re not always going to get what you want.”

“Are you calling me spoiled?”

“No,” Phainon says immediately. Then, “okay. Maybe. Yes.” After another beat of silence on Mydei’s end, he continues further. “I like your piece.”

“Is there any piece you don’t like?”

“I don’t really like Rite of Spring.”

“I know that’s a lie. You clearly just picked the obvious choice because you couldn’t think of a piece you actually don’t like.”

“Not true. I’m not a huge fan of Segerstam’s 81st Symphony.”

“Who the hell is that?”

“Weird guy. You could do without listening to it.”

Mydei sighs again. “Good night, Phainon. Maybe I’ll check it out.”

“Seriously, Mydei. There are much better composers you need to listen to before you get into the weird shit.”

“Good night, Phainon,” he says again, firmer this time. “I’ll see you tomorrow.”

Phainon yawns at the other end of the line. Mydei knew he had been asleep before he picked up. “Good night, Mydei.”

Mydei hangs up, slipping his phone into his jacket pocket. He sits at the bench, silent, for a few moments before making his decision. He grabs his sheet music off the stand and leaves, shoving it into his bag haphazardly as he does. What did Madam Herta’s approval matter, really? Phainon was always going to cheer for him.

“Mydei, look!” Phainon finds him as soon as he steps into the green room, shoving a stolen program in his face. “We’re next to each other!”

“What?” Mydei takes the program from him, analyzing the page it’s opened to. Sure enough, the piano section is arranged in alphabetical order by their last name, and he is right after Phainon. “Oh. I see.”

“I’ll stay backstage,” Phainon’s eyes are shining, with something akin to wonder as he looks at Mydei. “I’ll watch you. I promise.”

“I’d really rather you not,” Mydei mutters. “I’m going to embarrass myself in front of Madam Herta.” He’d seen her briefly as he made his way to the green room, exiting her office. She had given him a tiny nod, nothing more than that. Now, Mydei cares more about impressing Phainon than anything, but he doesn’t want to admit that.

“No, you’re not,” Phainon presses a hand to Mydei’s shoulder blade. “Just remember what we talked about yesterday. Did you find a reason to like

your piece?”

Mydei turns his head, looking at him for a few long moments. “Yeah,” he finally says, softly.

“Well, that’s great!” The edges of Phainon’s eyes crinkle as he grins. Mydei looks away.

“Phainon, can you help me with something?”

They both turn, met with someone Mydei doesn’t know. Before he can get a good look at him, Phainon is whisked away, apologizing quickly over his shoulder as they move to the empty piano in the corner.

Mydei’s heart starts to calm once he’s alone. He spots Hysilens unpacking her violin in the corner. He doesn’t know her very well, and usually wouldn’t spend his time speaking to people he’s not friends with, but he needs something to do with himself to offset his nerves.

Hysilens turns slightly as he approaches, in the middle of rosining her bow. “Finally lost him, did you?”

“Huh?” Mydei sits at one of the chairs beside her. “Who?”

“Phainon.” She puts her bow down, capping her rosin. “His clinginess is obvious to anyone with an ounce of perceptive ability. He talks about you all the time, you know. I’m surprised you’re ever afforded a moment alone when you’re in the same room.”

“Um, okay,” Mydei says, a little uncertain about how he’s supposed to take that. She sits back on her heels and plucks lightly at each of her violin strings. “If it’s that frustrating to everyone else, I can tell him to stop.”

“No, that’s okay.” She presses her ear closer to the strings, before reaching up to adjust her tuning pegs. “Does this sound right to you?” She plucks her A string, louder this time.

“I think so,” Mydei says. “You should ask Phainon if you want someone with perfect pitch to help you.”

“You should know what an A sounds like,” she answers, before moving to one of her other strings.

“So should you,” Mydei crosses his arms. “I’ve never tuned a piano in my life.”

“I’m tone-deaf,” Hysilens says blandly. She expertly continues to tune the rest of her strings by herself, so Mydei doesn’t comment on how he doesn’t think that’s true. “Anyways, I’m happy for you two. Without your generous services, Phainon would surely end up dying alone one day.”

Mydei’s unsure what that’s supposed to mean, but Hysilens has a tendency to say odd things, so he doesn’t question it too much. “I didn’t realize you and Phainon were so close,” he says, as she retrieves a thin rag from one of the compartments in her case and begins wiping down her strings.

“We met last year. I need an accompanist for a lot of the pieces I have to play, so it’s nice to have a pianist I’m friends with.”

“That’s good. I’m sure he’d be happy to play with you any time.”

She looks up at him, eyebrows scrunched together, and shakes her head. “Uh huh,” she starts. “We’re just friends, though.”

“I didn’t…” Mydei shifts his weight from side to side. He’s growing more uncomfortable with this conversation every second. “I didn’t say you weren’t?”

“I have a girlfriend. And I wouldn’t touch a man with a ten foot pole.”

“Okay?”

“So you and Phainon can keep each other to yourselves.”

Mydei swallows. Suddenly, he thinks he might know where this is going, and he doesn’t like the implications of any part of this conversation one bit. “Hysilens, are we…talking about the same thing?”

“Oh my god,” Hysilens mutters, setting her violin down carefully in her case. “You two aren’t dating?”

Mydei’s mouth falls open. Inexplicably, he feels his face heat up. “What— why would we be—?”

“Because he’s in love with you?” Hysilens supplies, like it’s obvious. “Do you have no intelligence outside of music?”

Mydei is suddenly overcome with a need to defend Phainon, because a statement such as that is so obviously defamation. “Phainon isn’t in love with me. We’re friends? Just like you two?”

“Just like us?” Hysilens laughs. “Phainon doesn’t talk about me 24/7. He doesn’t follow me around like a lost puppy and isn’t inconsolable when I’m more than a five minute walk away. He doesn’t look at me like…well, like that. And honestly, I would be disgusted if he did.” She stands, brushing dust off her black skirt, ignoring Mydei’s obvious bewilderment. “Now, get out of my way. I have to use the bathroom.”

Mydei steps aside, watching her leave. His heart is racing in his throat. He thinks his vision might black out, because he doesn’t notice Phainon until he’s right in front of him, waving a hand in his face.

“Hello-o-o, Mydei. Shit, what did she tell you? You look like your whole life philosophy was just turned upside down.”

“Not quite,” Mydei manages, throat dry. His voice is weak, but not as weak as he feels. Like he’d collapse like a newborn foal if he tried to walk.

Phainon laughs, collapsing into the chair Hysilens was just sitting in with as much comfort as if he were in his own house. “Don’t listen to her. She can be kind of intimidating.”

“Intimidating,” Mydei breathes. “Sure.” He refuses to look Phainon in the eye. He doesn’t want to know what he’d find.

“Want to go find a seat? They start in ten minutes.”

String solos open the concert, so pianists aren’t until the end. Mydei nods, and follows Phainon out of the green room.

Dating Phainon. That sounds…well, Mydei’s not quite sure. He’s never really thought about it before. Except in his dreams, perhaps, the details of which always seem to dissipate as soon as he wakes.

He wipes his sweaty palms on his dress pants. He needs to calm down.

Phainon leads him all the way down the hall until they reach one of the side entrances no one ever really goes through. He waves at the worker outside the door, and Mydei accepts a program of his own.

They climb all the way to the top, before settling in two seats off to the side that are part of a balcony. Mydei can’t see the stage very clearly unless he leans completely on the bannister, but it’s the least disruptive place to sit given that they have to leave halfway through.

“Oh! Look!” Phainon is shoving his program into Mydei’s face again, pointing at the first performer. “Hysilens is first.” He frowns. “Weird. I thought there were more violinists than just her and Kafka.”

He continues to ramble, something about Raiden Mei and her girlfriend, a bunch of people Mydei barely knows. He can’t find it in himself to pay attention. Not when Phainon’s knee brushes his and their elbows keep bumping like it’s casual. It would have been casual ten minutes ago. Now, Mydei has no idea what to believe.

Mydei tugs at the collar of his shirt, uncomfortable. He’s not even under the scorching hot stage lights, and he’s already sweating.

“Did you know a member of Hysilens’ string quartet is a high schooler?” Phainon finishes, propping his legs up on the bannister.

“Fascinating,” Mydei mutters. He wishes Phainon would just stop looking at him.

“I know, right? Talk about prodigy. Honestly, I’m surprised you didn’t start college when you were, like, fourteen.”

“Worked out for you, didn’t it?”

“Ha,” Phainon huffs, then goes eerily silent. Mydei can still feel his gaze on him. He leans back in his seat, closing his eyes. “Yeah. I guess it did.”

Mydei gulps. He can tell the house lights start dimming, so he opens his eyes and sits up. Thankfully, Phainon’s attention is on the stage now.

The head of the music department—Mydei has no idea what her name is, as he hasn’t spoken to her once—starts the concert by saying a few words, before exiting. Hysilens walks out moments later, violin in hand. There’s a moment of polite applause as she bows and adjusts her music stand that Mydei takes to look at the program.

He’s not familiar with violin repertoire at all, especially not when it comes to solo pieces. “Do you know this piece?” he whispers, turning to Phainon.

“You don’t know Erlkönig?” Phainon looks bewildered. Mydei shrugs. “Oh my god, prepare yourself. This piece changed my opinion on violin music entirely.”

Mydei shoots him a confused glance and settles back into his seat. He can hear Hysilens lightly pluck at her strings, ensuring they’re in tune. She starts playing shortly after that.

The piece is weird. Mydei is useless when it comes to string players and their technique, so he doesn’t expect to be overly impressed by her performance given that he doesn’t know what is difficult and what isn’t. In this case, it’s pretty easy to tell how incredibly talented she is, though.

There’s too much going on. With piano, you have ten fingers and seven octaves of notes at your disposal. It’s only natural that the hardest piano pieces would sound incredibly complicated. A violinist, though, has four fingers and four strings. There is no reason why Mydei should be hearing what sounds like three different instruments right now.

“What the fuck,” he breathes. Phainon snorts into his hand, before leaning in and resting his head on Mydei’s shoulder.

Mydei freezes. Hysilens’ performance, confusing as it was, had sufficiently wiped his brain of their earlier conversation, and with something as simple as Phainon leaning on him, it’s like the music is a thousand miles away.

It’s not out of the ordinary. Phainon is a very affectionate person, and Mydei, being his best friend, was no stranger to his physical affection. Now, though, he can’t help but wonder if it’s for an entirely different reason. What is Phainon like with his other friends? Touchier than Mydei, sure, but would he do this? Mydei doesn’t think so.

He swallows and tries not to appear as stiff as he feels. Phainon lifts one of his hands, settling it atop Mydei’s. “Are you alright?” he whispers, lifting his head so his chin rests on Mydei’s shoulder.

Mydei nods. Phainon’s gaze is so intense it feels like it’s burning holes through Mydei’s skull.

“Am I making you uncomfortable?”

“No,” Mydei says. Phainon accepts it, laying his head back down. Yes, Mydei thinks. He’s never been so unsure of himself before. He doesn’t know what he wants.

I’m happy for you two. Hysilens had thought they were dating. She thought Mydei reciprocated Phainon’s feelings, and it was obvious.

Mydei closes his eyes. He tries to pay attention to Hysilens’ performance, but it doesn’t work, no matter how starstruck he’s sure he would be. He can’t get her words out of his head. There’s a nauseous feeling in his gut, one he’s unfamiliar with, as he allows himself to think it over. Am I? He wants to throw up. Am I in love with Phainon?

The concert hall erupts into applause, and Mydei startles as he realizes that her piece has ended. He drops his program into his lap and joins them in

their applause. Phainon lifts his head from his shoulder to cup his hands over his mouth and whoop.

She bows, deep and graceful, and Mydei thinks he can see her shoot a grin at someone in the audience as she rises. He can count the number of times he’s seen her smile on one hand.

She walks off. The applause continues for a couple seconds before it finally subsides. Mydei feels bad for not listening as intently as he should’ve, given how impressive he had found her piece before Phainon ruined it all for him.

There are a few moments of silence. Mydei can’t quite see what’s going on onstage, until the doors open up and he can hear footsteps on the stage as light applause starts up again.

Mydei swallows. His hands are so sweaty, and he thinks that if they weren’t already curled into fists his fingers would be shaking.

Phainon is looking at the program, nodding slightly to himself as he undoubtedly recognizes the next piece and settles back into his seat.

He clears his throat. “Phainon—”

Perfectly on cue, the first few notes of the next piece ring out around them. He snaps his mouth shut, but it’s too late. Phainon is already looking at him, eyes wide with his unadulterated attention.

Mydei wets his lips. “Never mind,” he whispers.

Phainon’s eyebrows furrow together. “Are you sure you’re okay? You’re being weird.”

Mydei turns back around. “Watch the concert, Phainon.”

“We can leave,” Phainon suggests. “We can go back to the green room, if you want. I don’t really care about Kafka, and her piece is boring anyways —”

“Phainon.”

He closes his mouth. Mydei glares, for a moment, before they both turn back around.

They sit through the rest of the performances in silence. Kafka finishes her Bach piece. There’s one viola performance Mydei isn’t overly impressed by, and three cellists. If Mydei had to pick a favorite string instrument, it would be cello without a doubt, but he can’t even focus on the performances with Phainon next to him, practically simmering in their shared silence.

After the last cellist, they slip through the nearest exit as silently as possible after exchanging nothing more than a little nod.

Phainon is fourth, so they have some time before he has to be on stage. He immediately goes to speak with Hysilens, who is in the corner talking with Kafka and a tall, purple-haired cellist Mydei had just watched perform.

The last person Mydei wants to talk to is Hysilens right now, no matter how impressed he was by her performance. So he decides to sit at the piano instead, quietly going over a few rougher parts of his piece.

The first pianist comes back into the room. When Mydei looks up, Hysilens has moved away from the rest of the group, talking to Phainon in private. She glances his way. Mydei feels bile rise up his throat. He looks back down at the keys.

Some time during the third pianist’s performance, he can feel Phainon approach him before he sees him. He takes his hands off the keys and braces himself for whatever he’s about to hear.

“Mydei,” he starts, leaning over the lid. “Hysilens said—”

“Phainon.”

They both look up at the sound of Professor Anaxa’s voice, coming from where he stands in the doorway.

“Sorry, prof, two seconds, I promise—”

“Whatever you are talking about can wait. You’re needed now.” The third performer walks in behind him, and Phainon scrambles to grab his sheet music.

“Later, Mydei, I promise.” And then he’s gone, bolting out the door after Professor Anaxa.

Mydei sighs, and gathers his sheet music from the shelf before him. He looks over at Hysilens, but her back is turned to him, and she’s returned to her earlier conversation.

By the time he makes it to the backstage area, Phainon is already outside. Professor Anaxa leans against the door, watching the mini screen showing the main stage. There’s a tiny speaker that plays the outside audio, currently playing applause and the slight rustling as Phainon gets situated.

He takes a short moment of dramatic pause before he starts playing, and even outside the concert hall, through the shitty audio and vague background noises of him playing in the hall, Mydei is blown away by his prowess.

He’d only listened to Phainon’s étude once before, a recording of it after Phainon told him which one he was learning, but they’d never played them for each other before.

Beside him, Professor Anaxa is nodding along, tapping one of his fingers along with the tempo. Mydei’s eyes are glued to the tiny screen, trying to see as much of it as he can. He knows he needs to watch it back later. A thousand times, maybe. Until he can’t get it out of his eyes, or his ears.

He stares at Phainon’s hands, one flying across the keys as the other jumps around, playing tiny little chords. He doesn’t miss a single note, and doesn't stumble once. He stares at his black button down, sleeves rolled up just a little after his elbows, at the way the top button of his shirt is undone. His hair is messy, the little whorl on the top of his head bouncing back and forth as he moves his entire body with the music. He’s barely even sitting on the

bench anymore as he nears the end of the piece. He looks almost crazed as he plays the last chords, hands practically slamming against the keys.

Mydei’s throat feels dry. This, at least, finally isn’t a feeling he’s unfamiliar with. He finds people attractive all the time, and he’s believed Phainon to be stupidly handsome since the day that they met. But it was never like this. This wasn’t just attraction anymore—he wants to be by Phainon’s side forever.

He swallows regardless, heart hammering in his chest with a thousand emotions he can’t name as the concert hall erupts into applause.

“Thank you, Mydei,” Professor Anaxa says, from beside him.

Mydei still can’t take his eyes away from the screen, at the way Phainon tries to catch his breath as he stands. “For what?”

Phainon smiles from ear to ear as he bows, deep and long. Mydei has to bite his tongue to calm himself down. “He wouldn’t have been able to do this without you.” Is Professor Anaxa’s answer, one that Mydei cannot find a suitable reply to in the time it takes Phainon to walk from the center of the stage to the door.

He emerges, one hand pushing his sweaty hair out of his face. He’s still grinning, and it doesn’t even falter as he looks at Mydei.

“Good job, Phainon,” Professor Anaxa says. “That was, well. Perfect.”

“Thanks, Anaxa,” Phainon says easily. He looks at Mydei again, and something flickers across his face like there’s something else he wants to say.

He wouldn’t have been able to do this without you.

Mydei thinks he might know what Phainon wants to say. He can only hope it’s the same thing that he’s thinking, now—that Phainon is all he ever needed. That he’s the only person Mydei would ever have to play for that actually mattered.

Anaxa’s hand on his upper back drags him back to reality. “Good luck, Mydei,” he says. Phainon, still staring with something close to reverence on his face, nods.

The door opens. Mydei tightens his grip on his sheet music, and walks out.

The applause that sounds as he makes his way over to the piano sounds like it’s a thousand miles away. Mydei wants to look back, to catch just one more glimpse of Phainon on the other side of the door before it closes, but he pulls himself back to reality, stops before the piano, and bows. He doesn’t look at the audience as he rises. He doesn’t care anymore.

He sets up his sheet music on the rack, and sits down. He pulls up both his sleeves a little bit, and takes a deep breath as he sets his hands on the keys.

Mydei’s heart is pounding in his throat. He looks at the notes on the page, and it all seems like gibberish to him.

Something like a confession lingers longer in his brain than every other passing thought. You are in love with him. And then, fuck.

He can feel the audience’s tension. He doesn’t know how long he’s been sitting here, playing nothing. The stage lights beat down on him to an almost suffocating degree.

Phainon. Fuck.

He swallows. Closes his eyes. All he can see is Phainon’s white-blond hair and bright blue eyes, his dimples when he smiles, the sun tattoo on his neck.

He starts playing. It starts quiet, so quiet he can barely hear it. The audience is so silent it feels like he’s the only one here. Him, and Phainon. Behind that door. He’s watching, Mydei knows he is—he promised, and Phainon would never break his promise.

Mydei follows the notes on the page with perfect precision. He can’t remember the last time he made a mistake during a performance, but his

head is anywhere but where it needs to be right now. All he can think about is Phainon. He keeps playing.

He shuts his eyes, because he doesn’t need the notes anyway. He is so obviously in love with you. How couldn’t he tell? How did he need Hysilens to spell it out for him? Phainon always seemed to love him as easily as breathing. Ever since that first day he heard Mydei play, since the first time they got together outside of class. Things were always easy between them. Phainon befriended him in seconds and loved him quicker than that. He didn’t care about Mydei’s family. He didn’t care where he came from, or who he was. He gave Mydei a reason to keep playing, one he actually cared about. For the first time in his life, Mydei could see his future with perfect clarity. He would get this degree and become a pianist, and it didn’t seem so terrible anymore. All because Phainon would be right there with him, the whole time. Mydei is going to make sure of it.

The piece ends with a ritardando. He slows it down longer than he’d ever practiced, doesn’t count the perfect amount of time to hold out the last note. He does what he feels, what he thinks the piece needs. And when he finally lifts his hands, and opens his eyes, the lights are blinding. The sheet music before him is blurry. He relaxes, and the applause starts.

He sniffs. Wipes his nose, blinks tiny tears out of his eyes. He stands, facing the audience, really looking at them for the first time that night. He carefully gathers his sheet music off the rack, and bows. As he lifts his head, he spots Madam Herta off to the side. Mydei thinks his heart stops as they make eye contact for the briefest moment.

She gives him a tiny nod and lifts her hands in his direction. She’s clapping.

Mydei can’t help the ridiculous smile that breaks over his face. He practically bounces on the balls of his feet as he walks off stage, pushing the doors open.

They’re just barely closed when Phainon rushes towards him, nearly toppling him over with the force at which he hugs him. “Mydeimos,” he whispers, directly into his ear. “Kephale, you’re amazing.”

Mydei laughs wetly, and hugs him back.

“Good job, Mydei,” Professor Anaxa says. “I’m sure Herta is proud.”

“I think she approved,” Mydei answers, over Phainon’s shoulder. “Applause is a good sign, right?”

Phainon hugs him tighter, and then pulls away. “Of course she did,” he gushes, hands on Mydei’s shoulders.

“Cruel, that woman,” Professor Anaxa tuts, shaking his head. Phainon and Mydei move out of the way as he ushers the next student out the doors.

“Good job, Mydei,” she says, as she passes. “You too, Phainon.”

Mydei wishes her good luck as she exits, and the two of them head back down the hallway. “Do you want to watch the rest of the show?” Phainon asks. “Or—”

“No,” Mydei says immediately. “Balcony?”

“Balcony,” Phainon agrees instantly, grabbing Mydei’s hand and pulling him towards the elevator. Mydei’s palm is sweaty. He only hopes Phainon can’t notice it because his is sweaty, too.

The balcony is on the fifth floor of the music building, attached to the lounge near all the practice rooms. Mydei liked to spend his time there, doing homework outside when the weather was nice. It was probably his favorite place on campus, and was somehow almost always empty.

It is now, too, and so are most of the practice rooms, given that most people were either yet to perform tonight or had already. Thus, most had gone home or were inside watching.

Phainon finally lets go of his hand once they’re outside, both of them sitting on the bench overlooking the best view. It’s dark out, and the light from inside only barely illuminates Phainon’s face. Mydei faces him, one leg propped up on the bench, and the other hanging off the side. Phainon has his legs crossed, leaning back against the concrete wall.

“Are you ready for our theory exam tomorrow?”

Mydei has barely studied so far, and he knows that Phainon hasn’t either, even though he’d probably ace it anyway. That’s only one of the reasons why Mydei has no desire to talk about this right now. “Stop stalling.”

“Stalling what?” Phainon cocks his head to the side in mock innocence. Mydei nearly rolls his eyes. He can tell that under his light-heartedness is a touch of fear.

“Hysilens told me—”

“Mydei.” Phainon’s voice is firm. “Seriously, I can’t…I don’t want you to get the wrong idea.”

“Wrong idea?” Mydei raises an eyebrow. “I don’t think I am.”

Phainon forces a hand through his hair. “Look, Mydei, she didn’t know what she was talking about. She shouldn’t have told you that.”

“Told me what?” Mydei suddenly feels much less sure about this. “Say it, Phainon.”

“That I…I’m…” Phainon wets his lips. For the first time that night, he can’t seem to bring himself to look Mydei in the eye. “Mydei…don’t do this to me. Please.”

Mydei sits up. “Phainon,” he says, voice firm. “Tell me. Now.”

“Okay! Okay, I’m sorry…” Phainon fiddles with the hair at the back of his neck, the kind of gesture he usually does when he’s nervous. Mydei doesn’t take his eyes off him. “It’s just, I’ve never…I’ve never really, um, felt like this before.”

“Felt like what?” Mydei prompts, as gently as he can possibly muster. His voice is fighting to keep steady, and he can barely hear himself over the intense beating of his heart.

“Like…” Phainon’s free hand shakes as he lifts it to rest on his knee. Mydei reaches over and

places one of his hands on top of it, a gesture he hopes is soothing. “I,” he starts again, eyes wide and unblinking when he finally looks at Mydei, and isn’t too scared to look away. “I really like you,” he admits quietly. “More than I should.”

“How much do you think you should?” Mydei prods.

“As much as I like my friends,” Phainon swallows, so thickly that Mydei can hear it. “I don’t want to be your friend, Mydei. I never wanted that.”

Mydei bites his tongue. To think this had been going on for so long with Phainon, only for Mydei to realize it fifteen minutes ago. “And I…I don’t care if you feel the same or not, I really don’t. I just want you, by my side, and—and we can be friends if that’s all you want. I can be okay with that. Even though I don’t think I’ll ever really be able to move on.”

“Why wouldn’t I feel the same?” Mydei asks, dropping his leg off the side of the bench.

“You—” Phainon starts, then stops. Mydei lifts both his hands up to cup Phainon’s chin.

“I’m saying that I like you too, Phainon,” Mydei murmurs. “And I’ll go out with you, if that’s what you were trying to ask.”

“I—” Phainon starts. “I—yes, Mydei.”

Mydei presses closer. He wants to kiss him more than he’s ever wanted anything in his life, but Phainon’s obvious inexperience holds him back. “Can I—” he starts.

Phainon doesn’t let him finish. He leans all the way in, pressing his lips to Mydei’s with all the fervor and confidence of someone who knows exactly what they’re doing.

Mydei sinks into him, relishing in the feeling of Phainon’s lips on his. He’s warm, almost achingly so, even in the chilly evening air. His hands are the worst, burning his skin even through the fabric of his shirt, but Mydei can’t find it in himself to pull away, and he doesn’t think Phainon would let him if he tried. He kisses Mydei like he doesn’t need air.

Mydei almost can’t believe it’s his first kiss, but he knows it is. He gasps as they finally separate, Phainon’s lips bright red and slicked with spit, his eyes shining brighter than every star in the sky. “Mydei,” he breathes, voice ragged. He stares at Mydei like he’s starstruck. “God, I wanted you for so long.”

“How long?” Mydei asks. He wipes his lips dry on the sleeve of his shirt.

“You first?” Phainon prods, leaning back into him. His hands haven’t left Mydei’s waist, so hot Mydei vaguely thinks he might burn him.

“Ah…” Mydei bites his bottom lip. “About ten minutes, maybe.”

Phainon gapes. “You—what? When was that?”

“I was on stage.”

“Oh my god, Mydei,” Phainon laughs, forehead falling on Mydei’s shoulder. “I was wondering why you were taking so long to start.”

“Your fault for distracting me.”

“A good distraction, right?” He lifts his head, staring up at Mydei. “I would assume so, if your performance is anything to go off…”

“Yes,” Mydei assures him. “I thought of you, and then played what I felt.”

“Mydei,” Phainon whispers, then kisses him again. It’s shorter the second time, but the feeling lingers on Mydei’s lips for just as long. He wishes they had more time, that they weren’t technically in public right now. He wants Phainon to himself, now.

“They should be ending soon,” Mydei says, checking the time on his phone. “Do you want to go back downstairs?”

“No,” Phainon mutters, pouting. “I want to stay here with you.”

“You would still be with me downstairs,” Mydei stands up, forcing Phainon to pull his hands away. “Come on. Let’s go talk to people, and then you will come to my room.”

“Your room?” Phainon gets to his feet, perking up instantly. “Really?”

Mydei rolls his eyes. “Come on,” he says, pulling Phainon towards the door. He follows him all the way back to the elevator. “My roommate is gone, by the way,” he continues, a bit amused by the way Phainon instantly flushes bright red. “He went home this morning.”

Phainon presses close to Mydei’s side, his head burrowing in Mydei’s neck. “Stop it,” he murmurs. “You’re going to drive me crazy.”

Mydei doesn’t say anything, smiling to himself silently.

The elevator dings, and the doors open. The lobby is packed with people, enough to put a lump in Mydei’s throat. Part of him just wants to leave, but he needs to see Madam Herta one last time before the semester ends.

“Phainon!” Caelus bounds up to them almost immediately, his sister right behind him. There are a couple other people he came with—people from the marching band, which Mydei has done a good job avoiding up until this point. “And Mydei!” He looks down at their joined hands, and his eyes light up. “Fucking finally. Took you long enough, man,” he says, clapping a hand on Phainon’s shoulder.

Mydei tunes out the rest of their conversation, scanning the crowd around them. He spots Professor Anaxa talking to a couple of his other students, Hysilens with her violin case strapped over her shoulder walking out the door with a short girl at her side. He sees so many of his classmates, both in his music classes or history classes, that it makes him feel a little sick.

And then, finally, he notices Madam Herta, standing outside one of the stage doors talking to another woman. Mydei thinks he vaguely recognizes her as the one sitting next to her in the concert hall, but he wasn’t paying very close attention to anyone else.

“Be right back,” he says, mostly just to Phainon, letting go of his hand. He slips through the crowd, suddenly growing very nervous, as he approaches Madam Herta.

“Mydeimos!” she says, once she sees him. She smiles at him, for the first time in Mydei’s life, and a surge of pride runs through him. “Incredible job,” she says. “I was very impressed.”

“As was I,” the woman beside her adds. Mydei turns to look at her, wondering how he’s never seen her before. “Ruan Mei,” she explains, extending a hand to him.

Mydei takes it. “Mydei,” he says. “Thank you. It means a lot.” He has no idea who Ruan Mei is, but he’s sure she knows enough about music for Mydei to take it as a compliment if she’s hanging out with Madam Herta.

“Will I be seeing you in lessons next semester?” Madam Herta asks. It’s a pretty roundabout way of asking if he’s going to drop out, or switch professors. While that might be something he would have considered a few days ago, it’s not even a question in his mind now.

“Of course,” he answers. “I look forward to it.”

“As do I,” Madam Herta smiles again. “I do have high hopes for you, Mydeimos. You have real talent, we just have to figure out what it is that will unlock this talent.”

“Thank you,” Mydei says, flushing. “But I think I finally figured out what it is.”

“Perfect. Enjoy your summer, Mydeimos.”

“You too,” Mydei smiles again before he walks off, nearly bumping into Phainon in the middle of the crowd. Just setting eyes on him again is enough to send butterflies to his stomach—he can’t wait to get to his dorm. “Let’s go,” he says, grabbing Phainon’s hand and pulling him towards the door, ignoring all his protests.

“You’re way too eager, Mydeimos,” Phainon laughs, as they get outside. “Herta approved, then?”

“She’s never been so friendly in her life.”

“You don’t know that,” Phainon retorts. “Surely there are people out there that she loves.”

“Hm.” Mydei is skeptical, but then remembers the first time he noticed the ring on Madam Herta’s finger. Marriage, to someone like her, seems impossible. He had always just believed it was a stylistic choice. But then, the woman at her side—who else would you bring to a concert like this? Your friend? It wasn’t terribly unlikely. “Maybe,” he finally says.

“So,” Phainon changes the subject, as they walk down the path towards the dorms. “Am I allowed to stop at my dorm first?”

Mydei sighs, frustrated. He wants Phainon to himself now.

“I need to change!” Phainon protests. Mydei turns to look at him, in his concert black, and the idea of him changing out of it just frustrates him further. “And grab some stuff. Please, Mydei? I need my toothbrush.”

“Do you?” Mydei raises an eyebrow. “Your breath seemed just fine to me.”

Phainon flushes, going silent as Mydei swipes his ID at the door to his building. He pulls Phainon through the door as it unlocks, swiftly heading for the stairs. “Come on.”

“I’m coming, Mydeimos, you can relax!”

He drags Phainon all the way up two flights of stairs, and down the hall until he finally reaches his dorm room. His card takes what feels like

forever to read, and as soon as it beeps he nearly pushes the door down with the force he uses to open it.

The lights are off. He doesn’t care to turn them on and pushes Phainon against the closed door, claiming his lips once more.

Phainon makes a surprised noise, immediately trying to match Mydei’s energy as he kisses him back. “Mydei—” he manages, between kisses. Mydei doesn’t care. He licks into Phainon’s mouth, muffling any words he might have wanted to say, as he fumbles with Phainon’s dress shirt and pulls it out from where it’s tucked into his pants. He runs his hands underneath, feeling the soft outline of his abs. He might have only just figured out he was in love with him, but the attraction had been there ever since their first session together at the gym.

Mydei pulls away so he can vaguely make out where the buttons start on his shirt, reaching for the first one. “Mydei, wait—” Phainon tries again. Mydei kisses him again, before finally drawing back.

“Stop talking,” he mutters, undoing the first button, then lowering his hands to the second.

“I—I’m not—” Phainon starts.

The realization washes over Mydei like a bucket of cold water. He drops his hands. Takes a tiny step back. “Oh,” he says, softer this time. In his haze, he had forgotten all about Phainon’s lack of experience. It was just so difficult to believe. “I’m sorry. I got ahead of myself.”

“No,” Phainon nearly whines, stepping forward. “I want to, of course, I just —you’re so…and I’m…”

“Use your words.”

Phainon sighs, frustrated. “I just feel like I won’t be able to give you what you want?”

“What?” Mydei crosses his arms. “I don’t care, Phainon. I just want you.”

“Oh…” Phainon whispers.

Mydei presses a hand to his cheek. “Phainon,” he says firmly. “Do you want to do this? Yes or no.”

“Yes,” Phainon’s response is instantaneous. “Yes, of course.”

“Okay,” Mydei says. “Then come on.” He pulls Phainon towards his bed, flicking the desk light on as they go. He pushes Phainon down, before climbing on top of him and resuming his work on his shirt buttons until he finally frees him completely. Then, he moves to fumble with his belt buckle, while Phainon attempts to undo Mydei’s own shirt.

Phainon’s fingers are shaking so violently that he can’t even loosen a single button. Mydei laughs as he swats his hands away, electing to do it himself while he watches. “Sorry,” Phainon murmurs.

Mydei ignores him, tugging his shirt off over his head once he loses his patience. He tosses it aside, and it lands somewhere on the floor.

Mydei settles over Phainon’s lap, rolling his hips gently as he leans down to nip at Phainon’s neck tattoo. “Mydei—” Phainon gasps, breath hot as it puffs against Mydei’s ear. He shivers, kissing along the junction of Phainon’s throat and over the thin line decorating his chest.

“Why did you get this?” Mydei whispers, running his finger across it. Phainon’s whole body trembles beneath him.

“The sun,” Phainon breathes. “Praise the sun,” he shudders.

“Praise the sun,” Mydei repeats. “Is that a reference to ancient Okhema?” He leans back, sitting over Phainon’s hips. His nails dig into his thighs, and he ignores the dull pain.

Phainon nods. “The Deliverer,” he whispers. “Cyrene always told me I reminded her of him.”

Mydei smiles a little, amused. “Really? That’s rather presumptuous of you.”

“Ha—” Phainon huffs, halfway to a laugh. “Blame Cyrene, then.”

“Well then, Deliverer,” Mydei says, splaying his hands over Phainon’s chest. “Are you just going to sit there, or are you going to do something?”

“Don’t call me that,” Phainon says. He blushes all the way to his shoulders. Despite both his inexperience and embarrassment, he braces one hand on the back of Mydei’s neck and flips their positions in one smooth motion.

Mydei gasps softly as his head hits the pillow, heat instantly pooling in his gut at the sight of Phainon hovering above him. He bites his tongue as he wills his racing heart to calm down.

“Wait,” Phainon says suddenly, and sits back on his heels. He rummages through his pockets, pants still halfway undone, and pulls out his phone. “Do you have a playlist?”

Mydei freezes. “What?”

“A…a playlist,” Phainon repeats. His blush creeps even further down his chest.

“A playlist,” Mydei deadpans.

“Yeah.”

“What the hell are you talking about?” A little bit of Mydei’s arousal is starting to fade. “A sex playlist?”

“Yeah,” Phainon says, unashamed. “That.” Okay—maybe a little bit ashamed.

Mydei blinks. “No. Phainon. I don’t have a sex playlist.”

“Huh,” Phainon wonders aloud, still navigating somewhere on his phone. “Weird. I totally thought you would, given that you’ve done this before.”

“Most people don’t have a sex playlist.”

“Untrue,” Phainon says, turning up the volume on his phone. An ad starts to play at full volume.

Mydei covers his face with his hands. “Why you?” He laments, voice muffled.

“Hey,” Phainon says, as he skips the ad. “It’s not my fault you’re in love with me.”

Mydei starts to say something, but it’s muffled by Phainon pressing their lips together after tossing his phone off to the side. He can’t hear the song yet. He’s not sure he wants to know what he chose.

“Oh my god,” he manages, as Phainon lowers himself to kiss slowly along Mydei’s jaw, and Mydei starts to recognize the first few notes of an orchestral piece. “Phainon,” he says, through his breathy laughter partially due to the sensation of Phainon kissing his neck. “You are…the corniest person I have ever met.”

“Again,” Phainon murmurs, against his skin. “You’re the one in love with me.”

“Rach 2?” Mydei nearly wheezes. “You seriously want to—”

“I love you,” Phainon answers, voice so earnest that Mydei can’t find it in himself to make fun of him anymore. “And I love this piece. And so do you, you admitted it yourself last time I played it for you—”

“Because you love it,” Mydei says. “Because it reminds me of you.”

“Mydei…” Phainon whines, shoving his face into Mydei’s neck. “You can’t just say something like that.”

“Come on.” Mydei shoves a leg between Phainon’s thighs, and he thinks the noise Phainon makes in response would play on repeat in his brain for days. “I already lost my patience five minutes ago.”

It doesn’t last very long. Phainon lays curled into Mydei’s side, both of them naked as they catch their breaths while the climax of the song plays

around them. “I love you,” Phainon whispers into Mydei’s neck. “You don’t even understand what I would do for you.”

Mydei pulls him in closer, and kisses the top of his head. “Actually, I think I do,” he murmurs. He would do the same, without a second thought.

Mydei has almost drifted off when Phainon speaks again, voice reverberating against his chest. The playlist has moved on, halfway through a different symphony completely unlike Rach 2. He thinks it sounds a little like Shostakovich.

“I’m going to play it one day,” Phainon says, decidedly.

“I don’t think this piece has a piano part,” Mydei mumbles into his hair. His eyes are still closed. He feels Phainon’s answering laugh more than he hears it.

“Not Shostakovich, Mydeimos,” he answers, and Mydei internally congratulates himself for being able to recognize composers better now. “Rach 2. I’m going to play it one day.”

“Okay,” Mydei says.

“Promise me you’ll be there when I play it.” He can feel Phainon reach one of his hands up Mydei’s chest, before settling against his chin. He threads his fingertips through Mydei’s hair, pushing it behind his ear. “And I’ll be there when you’re selling out stadiums and have three charting rock albums.”

Mydei thinks about his own realization earlier that day, on stage. How he thought, for the first time in his life, that he could actually build a life for himself around piano. And then Madam Herta’s words. You have real talent. If she thought so, how could he waste it on rock music? Even if he loved it more than he would ever love piano music, whether or not Phainon was there. Someone he loved could only do so much, Mydei thinks.

His dream life would be one where he could have rock, and Phainon could have classical, and they were able to live together. But that would never

happen.

“You think I’m going to be a rockstar?” he asks.

“I think you’re a gift to the world,” Phainon says immediately. “Whatever it is, then. Whatever music you make. I’ll be there.”

“Okay,” Mydei hums, lifting his own hand to curl his fingers through Phainon’s soft locks of hair.

“Promise,” Phainon says again. “Promise me you’ll be there.”

Mydei opens his eyes. He lifts his head a little, met with Phainon’s pleading gaze, and finds that he can’t deny him anything. Not that he would ever consider any other future. Not that he would ever be faced with Phainon’s dreams and tell him no. He rests his head back against the pillow.

“I promise.”

October 3869. Eight months before the release of Oracle.

With their deadline growing closer and Phainon growing healthy enough to live relatively independently, the band takes a couple weeks off from writing to start recording with Ratio. Mydei was unsure of how it would work originally, but was pleasantly surprised by how much Ratio seemed to trust them. And even though Cipher has production knowledge and capabilities, he wouldn’t trust her to touch the production software with a ten foot pole.

City of Thieves is the first song they finish, and hearing Caelus’ trumpet solo altogether with the rest of it for the first time is enough to put a stupid grin on his face. Cipher snaps a photo of him that he sees later on her social media, in a slideshow with several other photos from the recording process. Her caption remains artfully cryptic, but the comments speculate nonetheless. One that sticks out to him reads “wow i’ve literally never seen mydei smile. this album is about to EAT”. Unnecessary comment about the frequency of his smiles aside, Mydei is inclined to agree. This is, without a doubt, the best collection of music he’s ever written.

Ratio agrees. The more songs they finish, the more praises he has to give. Mydei gets the sense that he doesn’t have enough of those to go around, so he’s more than happy to be the one to accept them.

Even with the break, though, Mydei can’t stop himself from writing. He doesn’t want to leave any idea untouched, and the one person in his closest circle that he’s never written a song about was his mother.

He could never bring himself to do it. He couldn’t even bring himself to write music in the months after her death, and by the time he was recording with Castorice and Cipher he didn’t know them well enough to tell them about something like that.

Now, though, he’s made peace with her death. He no longer spends his nights agonizing over what he could have done differently. He no longer feels guilty quitting piano, because he knows she would be equally proud of the success he’s gotten himself now.

He spends weeks on this song alone, changing lyrics here and there and scratching out parts of the score until it’s finally perfect. It’s not a sad song,

not really—he’s glad, if anything, that he wrote it now rather than when he was mourning her.

He calls it Conqueror of Lions and when he finally performs it to the band, on a stripped back version just on piano, he gets tears out of both Hyacine and Castorice. Cipher is close, he thinks, with the way she’s made herself tiny in the corner of the couch and doesn’t say much when he’s done.

“Your mother sounds like an amazing woman,” Hyacine says, stepping back when she’s finished hugging him. “I’m sad I never got to meet her.”

“You would have loved her,” Mydei says. He’s near tears, too, and the unsteadiness of his voice is hiding nothing. “All of you would’ve. Actually, I don’t know how anyone couldn’t.”

Hyacine laughs, then moves to the whiteboard and uncaps a pink marker. Their list of songs is in a disorganized jumble to the left of the board, while on the right they have a working tracklist. Cipher’s pitch of thirteen songs is the highest anyone had thought, so it goes to thirteen, even though none of the songs have a spot on it yet.

Hyacine writes Conqueror of Lions in the thirteenth slot, at the very end.

“The last song?” Mydei asks, standing from the piano to linger behind her. “Really?”

“Does anyone object?” Hyacine turns, pointing the marker at Castorice, and then Cipher.

Castorice shakes her head. “No. I think it’s perfect.”

Cipher doesn’t object either, so it stays.

He’s just dropped Phainon off at physical therapy the next week when he gets a text from Cipher alone out of nowhere. She’s his friend, of course, but far from his closest friend in the band, so she rarely texts him alone.

Cipher Today 11:58

i have an hour of freedom.
