ur dumb as bricks go there

ok

The location in question turned out to be a cafe in the middle of the city, no more than five minutes from Phainon’s physical therapist. He parks his car on the side of the road and enters the cafe, greeted instantly by the smell of coffee and bells jingling as the door shuts behind him.

There are a couple of people sitting down inside, and one barista who smiles at him as he enters. He musters a smile back—which probably doesn’t look as friendly as he imagines it does—and scans the cafe for any sign of Cipher.

Nothing. He’s about to pull out his phone to check he got the location right when someone taps him on the shoulder and appears in front of him, like magic.

“What the hell?” he sputters. “Where did you come from?”

Cipher flashes him a toothy grin. “Jumped through the roof,” she shrugs. “Come on, little prince. We got a lot to talk about.”

“Do we?” he asks faintly, following her as she approaches the barista at the counter.

“One triple shot espresso and one of your massive brownies, please,” she asks, pulling out her wallet. Mydei eyes the disaster that’s inside of it and shudders.

“Alright,” the barista says, tapping at his screen. “Are you two together?”

“Oh, no, no,” Cipher cackles, patting Mydei on the shoulder so hard he fears it might leave a mark. “He can pay for himself. Can’t you?” She coos, turning to Mydei.

“Cipher,” Mydei groans, rubbing at his forehead. To think he’s about to spend an hour alone with her is already driving him crazy.

The barista smiles awkwardly at that, and Cipher pays with a crumpled ten dollar bill. She makes a show of telling him to keep the change that Mydei knows is just because she’s too lazy to carry around coins, and Mydei steps up to order next as she finds a table.

“Sorry about her,” he murmurs, apologetic. “Do you have pomegranate juice?”

He ends up ordering a seasonal latte and approaches Cipher’s table as the barista works on their orders. “What kind of a cafe is this?” he complains, shedding his coat on the spare chair and sitting down across from her. “They don’t even have pomegranate juice.”

“No cafe outside of Kremnos would serve you pomegranate juice, you freak,” Cipher scoffs. “Barista was cute, wasn’t he?”

“What?” Mydei turns, eyeing him as discreetly as possible. His back is turned, messing with the espresso machine, so Mydei isn’t sure. He looks like he has some muscle underneath his apron, though, so he shrugs. “I mean, I guess.”

“Oh my god,” Cipher groans. “You’re not even checking people out without my help? Hopeless, you are.”

“Why the hell did you bring me here?” Mydei hisses, leaning over the table. “To talk about my love life? Seriously?”

“Geez, someone’s peeved,” Cipher holds up her hands in surrender. “I just thought I’d try to help a guy out, y’know?”

“I’m not peeved,” Mydei leans back, crossing his arms. “And I don’t need help in that area.”

“Clearly,” Cipher rolls her eyes. “I mean, look at you.”

“Triple shot espresso,” the barista says, sliding Cipher’s order across the table at her. “And your brownie,” He slides over a brownie that takes up the entire plate, and Mydei wonders how often Cipher frequents this cafe to know about their “massive brownie”. She seems more like the type of person to be a regular at a strip club than a cafe.

“And a pumpkin latte, for you,” he says to Mydei, giving him his coffee.

“Thank you,” Mydei says. The barista smiles and walks away.

“He’s totally into you,” Cipher says, the second he’s out of earshot.

“You think he’s into me because he smiled at me,” Mydei hisses. “Do you even hear how ridiculous you sound?” He picks up the spoon placed on the plate underneath his latte mug, and begins to stir it around.

“You only think that because you can’t understand social cues,” Cipher rolls her eyes. “Again, dude, look at you.”

Mydei closes his eyes, leaning further back into his seat. “I don’t know what you mean by that, and I’m not sure I want to,” he says, chewing at his lower lip.

“Dude,” Cipher says. “You’re, like, hot.”

An itching feeling climbs up the back of Mydei’s neck. He grimaces. “What?”

“Oh my god,” Cipher mutters, rolling her eyes. “Modest son of a bitch. You’re smoking, dude. I mean it.”

“Cipher,” Mydei groans, covering his face with his hands. Their sexualities had not exactly been a common point of conversation, but he was certain Cipher didn’t swing that way. “I thought you were a lesbian?” He whispers, leaning forward a little bit. He can only hope Cipher picks up the hint and lowers her voice.

“Uh, yeah?” she says, like that was obvious even with this conversation. “And I’m telling you you’re hot as fuck. So you should take it as a double compliment.”

“Please stop calling me that—”

“There’s something feminine about you,” Cipher continues. “I think that might be it. I haven’t quite been able to place my finger on what it is, though—”

“Stop.”

“—given that you’re six feet tall and pure muscle—”

“Cipher, please,” he begs, and she finally closes her mouth. “You can stop. I know my assets.”

“Oh my god, are you serious?” She’s getting dangerously close at this point, leaning more over the table with every word that she says. One of her sweatshirt strings is hanging into her coffee, but Mydei isn’t going to tell her about it as punishment for putting him through this conversation. “Your assets? Are you even a real person?”

“All I’m saying,” Mydei groans, “is that I know they like it when I take my shirt off.”

“Oh, you think your abs are the moneymaker? No, pretty boy, your torso would mean nothing if it wasn’t attached to that gorgeous face.”

“You have to stop.”

“Pretty boy. That’s so fitting. I bet, when you were bullied in high school, they loved to call you that.”

“I wasn’t bullied in high school.”

“HA! You were a classical pianist, and you want me to believe that?”

“I went to a music school. Can we move on now?”

“Fine, you win,” Cipher acquiesces, leaning back in her seat. She watches her hoodie string fall out of the cup and puts it in her mouth. “All I’m saying is you could have anyone you want, and you’re choosing… celibacy?” She shakes her head. “That wasn’t even in the list of options.”

“I never said I was celibate,” Mydei mutters.

“...Okay, ew…”

“Just that I don’t want a relationship right now. Is that so hard to believe?”

“No,” Cipher starts, and Mydei foolishly thinks for a second that he might have gotten through to her. “Because I know there’s someone you want.”

Mydei sighs, bracing himself.

“But I bet you’d want a relationship with them, though. Or should I say him?”

“Cifera—”

“You know I’m right,” Cipher’s voice is infuriatingly smug. “You weren’t even over that boy for a day. You can tell yourself all you want that you’re only happy for the chance to reconnect with an old friend, but you know the truth deep down. You know you want him back, that you’re in love with him, and have been for years.”

Mydei hangs his head. He doesn’t know why he can’t even tell her she’s wrong.

“Do you need me to clarify who I’m talking about?”

Mydei still doesn’t answer. Of course he doesn’t. But admitting that would only prove her point, and it’s too late to act confused.

“Phainon, Mydei. You’re in love with that pianist.”

“Why don’t we ever talk about your love life?” Mydei retorts, lifting his head. His hair hangs into his face, and he shakes it out of his eyes.

Cipher rolls her eyes. “Going great, pretty boy. Out of the two of us, I’m not the emotionally constipated one.”

“Oh, wow. You calling me emotionally constipated. That’s a first.”

“In these matters, yes. When I like someone I tell them.”

“You’re a terrible liar.”

“I’m an incredible liar,” Cipher scoffs. “See, just now, when you accused me of lying, you were right. Except you think I’m lying about the wrong thing.”

“Okay,” Mydei says, reaching for his drink as he attempts to decipher what she was actually lying about. He finds it’s too difficult, met with her elusive blue eyes. “Who’s the last person you liked, then?”

Cipher takes a very long sip of her drink through the straw. “No one you’d know,” she mumbles, when she’s done.

“How am I meant to trust a single thing you say?” Mydei throws his hands in the air, a little frustrated. He hates liars, which is why he had so much trouble getting along with Cipher when they first met. “Who is it? Who do you know that I wouldn’t, at least tangentially?”

“You don’t know my life,” Cipher answers.

“Cas?”

“No.”

“Hyacine.”

“No.”

“Fuck. Okay. Hysilens.”

“Hysi—no.”

“Hysilens’ little girlfriend.”

“Don’t call Cerydra little. No.”

“Robin.”

“What the fuck? No.”

“I’m out of girls. Phainon.”

“Phainon,” she deadpans. “Believe me, Mydei, he’s all yours.”

“Either you really do know other people, or you’re lying to me.”

“Wonder which one it is.”

“Stelle. Do you even know her?”

“Of course I know that little freak. No.”

“Cyrene.”

“Stop, Mydei.”

“March. Or her twin, the evil one.”

“You’re just pulling random people out of your ass, at this point,” Cipher closes her eyes, pressing her palms together like she’s praying. “If I tell you, will you stop?”

“Obviously?”

“It’s someone you already mentioned.” Cipher stares down at the wooden table between them, like the flimsy plastic menu is suddenly a lot more interesting.

“I knew it,” Mydei says, then thinks back to everyone he mentioned. “It’s Cas, isn’t it?”

“You totally believed me when I said no, though.”

“Holy shit,” Mydei breathes. He had believed her. In fact, he was so certain it must have been Castorice, that he was surprised when her “no” sounded true. “How long?”

“Enough about me,” Cipher says, waving her hand side to side. Mydei can sense the tiniest bit of fear in her voice. “Phainon. The real important part of this conversation.”

“I think you being in love with one of our bandmates is much more important.”

“Did I say in love?” Cipher feigns innocence, looking anywhere but at Mydei. “I don’t think I did. But you, Mydei, are in love.”

“I’m not, and I’m serious,” Mydei says, placing his elbows on the table and leaning over at her. “Seriously, Cipher. I’ve been over Phainon for years.”

“Hm,” Cipher pouts a little, lifts her cup to her mouth, and takes a tiny sip. She savors it in her mouth for a while before responding. “Yeah, okay. I believe you.”

Mydei sighs. “Now I can tell you’re lying.”

Cipher gasps. “Wow, good job, Mydei! You’re learning!”

Mydei can’t stand sarcasm on most days, but he always finds himself less irritated by Cipher’s because he can always, at least, tell that she’s being

sarcastic. He would say she makes her sarcasm more obvious around him on purpose, but he thinks that might be giving her too much credit.

“You can deny it all you want, but you should think about it,” she says, ripping a corner off her brownie and stuffing it in her mouth. She continues to talk around it. “It would do great things for our song tally if you could finally write some damn love songs.”

“Or you could,” Mydei suggests. “About Cas.”

“I will do no such thing,” Cipher says, swallowing her brownie. “But I am here to talk music.”

“Ah,” Mydei nods. “So all the bullshit about me being in love with my best friend was just, what, to throw me off?”

“Stop calling him your best friend before you really piss me off,” Cipher scoffs. “I’m getting serious now.”

“Oh,” Mydei raises an eyebrow, “okay.”

“I want a song,” she confesses. “Like,” she swallows, lacing her fingers together on the table in front of her. “I want to sing one.”

“Wait, seriously?” Mydei pushes his latte aside. He doesn’t have a problem with any of his bandmates being the main vocalist on a track instead of him, he just always assumed they didn’t want to. To think it would be Cipher, of all people, to volunteer herself first, throws him off.

She nods. “There’s this song that I think I need to write,” she says. “I thought we could write it together, and then both of us could sing it.”

“You can sing and play bass at the same time?” Mydei asks.

Cipher sighs. “Not…currently.”

“Okay,” Mydei says. “I see no problem if you think you could learn. What are you going to write about?”

“My, um…mother,” she admits, then sighs, leaning back in her seat in frustration. “You inspired me, okay? I’ve been such an asshole to Aglaea, when it could be so much worse. She could be dead.”

“Yeah?” Mydei starts, a little uncomfortable. “I guess she could?”

“You want to know,” Cipher says. Her tone isn’t accusatory, but Mydei feels like it might as well be. She sighs, sitting up straight in her chair. “Aglaea adopted me when I was thirteen,” she begins. “I was a shit kid, and an even worse teenager. I don’t know how she handled it, and one day, all my bullshit caught up to me, I guess.”

“She kicked you out?!” Mydei demands, incredulous.

“Not really,” Cipher says. “We had a huge argument, I was probably screaming at her. Aglaea never showed many emotions—cold as ice, as always—and it’s infuriating to be faced with nothing when you’re so pissed off you feel like you’re losing it. So I left, and didn’t go back for years.”

Mydei knows they must have reconciled at some point, since he and Castorice were allowed to stay there while they recorded their first EP.

“You know, I was just never the kind of kid a woman like her should’ve had,” Cipher continues. “I was a piece of shit. Had been my whole life. By the time she adopted me, she wasn’t going to be able to just…discipline that away. I felt like I belonged on a sidewalk, not in a mansion. We never really saw eye to eye on most things. She had her tailor shop, modeling agency, orchestra—nothing I was any fit for. I started the double with her guidance. She never said it out loud, but I know she hated when that switched to electric. When I started playing rock music.”

That must have been the reason Aglaea seemed so disdainful while they were there. Maybe she wanted them to start a string quartet, instead. Mydei almost laughs at the thought.

“I guess today, we’re kind of on good terms,” she says. “I just don’t talk to her or visit very often, because I don’t want to ruin the truce we have. She doesn’t push anything because she thinks that’s what I want. I know she

doesn’t approve of the life I’m living, but today, it’s more okay than it was when I was a teenager.”

“God,” Mydei breathes. “That is complicated.”

“Not really,” Cipher says, back to chewing on her hoodie string. “I know I’m wrong for how I’ve handled all of this.”

“Well, you’re a lot more self aware about all this than I was expecting.”

“So now you’re just calling me an ass. Thanks, Mydei.”

Mydei shrugs, because he sort of was, and isn’t going to deny it. “Anyways, your song. What do you have planned so far?”

As it turns out, she doesn’t have anything past the idea. Mydei is beginning to wonder how much of Cat Food was her contribution and how much of it was Castorice’s, at this point.

They don’t get that much done before Mydei has to leave, but it’s enough of a starting point for Mydei to work on instrumentals on his own time.

When he picks Phainon up after this meeting, he feels like he’s looking at him differently. There’s something about him as he climbs into the passenger seat and closes the door behind him that forces Mydei to pull his gaze away.

He’s been getting better. It’s slow, but he has more movement in his hands today than he did three weeks ago. He doesn’t shut down after physical therapy anymore, but Mydei can still see the presence of a deep sadness in his eyes.

Mydei thinks Cipher’s interrogation was pointless, because Mydei knows that he loves Phainon. He always has. Only now, he’s not really sure what that means for him.

They finish recording all the songs they have written on Halloween. It’s a much bigger holiday in Penacony than anywhere else, as far as he knows, so he doesn’t think much of it when he heads to the studio in the morning. Ratio walks into the room with some sort of wizard’s hat on, grumbling something about company policy before immediately taking it off.

All they have left to do is touch ups, re-recording some backing vocals, and adding finishing touches to any parts that feel like they’re missing something. It’s still somewhat early in the afternoon when they leave, and Mydei can’t wait to go to the gym and take a hot bath afterwards.

Unfortunately, though, all of his plans crumble the moment they make their way out of the studio.

“Excuse me, where do you think you’re going?” Cipher asks in the parking lot, when he breaks away from the group to go to his car.

“What?” Mydei unlocks the doors, hearing it click. “Home?”

“No you are not. You’re coming with us to the Halloween store.”

“The Halloween store,” Mydei deadpans. “Very funny, Cipher. Bye.”

“It’s a real thing,” Hyacine supplies, looking at least a little more apologetic than Cipher. “Aren’t you coming to the party tonight?”

“The party,” Mydei looks between the three of them, sensing no sarcasm. He’s never been more confused in his life. Maybe ignoring Halloween was just a Kremnoan thing?

“When was the last time you checked your DMs?” Castorice asks. Her voice sounds a little faint.

Mydei wracks his brain. Really, he has been almost completely offline ever since the photos of him and Phainon first started circulating. He’d open it here and then, but actually checking his messages was a completely different thing. “A long time ago,” he answers. “Are you seriously telling

me you guys have been planning a party and haven’t mentioned a thing to me in person?”

“It’s not our party,” Hyacine says. “We were just invited.”

Mydei blinks. “I was invited.”

“Why would we be invited and you wouldn’t be?”

Mydei sighs, leaning back against his car door. “Do I have to go? Who’s party is it?”

“The Astral Express,” Cipher says. “They’re in the area this month. It’s in Sunday Oak’s east coast mansion.”

Any inkling of desire Mydei might have had to attend this party instantly dissipates. “Do I have to go?” Mydei asks again, voice near whining. He really doesn’t want to do anything less.

“Yes,” Cipher says, grabbing his wrist. She starts dragging him over to her car, and Mydei starts to wonder what excuses he could possibly make to get out of this. “It’s good for meeting people in the industry.”

“How many people are going to be there?”

“Phainon can come,” is Cipher’s idea of a suitable response, as she opens the passenger door and shoves him inside.

“Cipher. How many people?”

“It’ll be small!”

They go back to his apartment after the “Halloween store”, which was very much real, to get ready together. Mydei had bought Phainon a costume too, set on at least having him there so they could suffer through it together.

Cipher and Castorice both have similar costumes. They’re both zombies, with similar makeup styles, except Cipher is in a suit, Castorice in a white dress. It looks a lot like a couples costume, and while neither of them say anything about it being such, Mydei can’t help but remember what Cipher had said a couple weeks back when they first met up to work on the new song.

Hyacine is a witch, though not of the evil sort. She wears a short black dress with pink accents, ties her hair into pigtails, and puts on a pointy hat. She even has a little wand to go with it that she attaches to the belt of her dress.

Mydei’s costume is a vampire—not his decision, but rather theirs. Hyacine slicks his hair back with a disturbing amount of gel, Castorice paints his face several shades paler, gives him dark circles, and blood-red lips. He hates the way the fake fangs feel in his mouth but is eventually convinced to leave them in at least for the beginning of the party.

Phainon is getting dressed while Mydei gets his make up done, and he nearly drops his phone as he walks into the living room area when it’s his turn. “Oh,” he says eloquently. “You look…good, Mydei.” His eyes are wide open, blushing furiously. Mydei swallows down the undeniable realization that Phainon seemingly reciprocates his lingering feelings of attraction.

But attraction doesn’t mean anything. It doesn’t mean Phainon is in love with him, and it doesn’t mean Mydei is in love with Phainon.

Besides, Mydei doesn’t think he hides it any better, with the way he gawks at Phainon’s waist in the pirate costume he had picked out. Maybe he picked it on purpose, maybe not. That was his secret to keep.

They end up arriving an hour late, around ten, and the party has very much started by then. It is by no means small. Mydei instantly feels out of his depth, and can only hope Castorice and Hyacine have done a good enough job making him unrecognizable.

They can see the flashing lights and hear the DJ from almost a mile away, but it’s somehow a thousand times louder the second they enter.

Caelus greets them immediately, dressed as a superhero from a comic Mydei only vaguely recognizes—he was never very interested in superheroes.

“You made it!” he says, grinning ear to ear. Mydei thinks he’s mainly talking to Phainon, but they were all invited, so it’s not like he’s too out of place. “Phainon, how have you been? Getting better?”

“Slowly,” Phainon says sheepishly. “My hands are really ugly, though. Hence the gloves.” He lifts both his hands up to show him. The gloves only look a little out of place with his costume, but Mydei still thinks it would have been better without it. It was Phainon who insisted on wearing them.

“Ah, you’re still sexy, though,” Caelus says, with a wink. Mydei shoots Cipher a confused glance and leaves that conversation there, disappearing into the crowd.

Cipher follows close behind him, cackling. “You don’t think they were flirting, do you?”

“Of course not,” Mydei snaps. “Caelus is straight as a board. I need a drink.”

“Pfft, I wouldn’t be too sure about that, little prince,” Cipher finally catches up, falling into step beside him as he tries to find the food. “He’s had his fair share of homoerotic relationships.”

“How the hell would you know?”

“I know everything about everything.” Cipher steps in front of him, then, pulling him by his jacket sleeve directly over to the drinks table. “Use your eyes, dude. Not that hard.”

Mydei takes a long, deep breath, and begins to pour himself some punch. He doesn’t know if it’s spiked, but he hopes it is.

“I’m going to make shit happen with Cassie tonight,” Cipher confesses out of the blue.

Mydei immediately misses his cup and pours punch all over his hand. He curses, grabbing a nearby napkin and patting himself down. “What?” he asks. “Seriously?”

“Yeah,” Cipher says, overconfidently. “Watch and learn, heart eyes.”

“Heart eyes,” he looks at her, unimpressed. “That might be the worst one yet.”

“They’re your eyes, not mine,” she shrugs. “Seriously, though. You don’t think she, like, doesn’t like me, right?”

“I don’t know,” Mydei tells her. “According to you, I can’t even recognize my own feelings, so I’m not sure I’m the best person to ask something like that.”

“Shit, you’re so right…” she chews on her lip, staring off into the crowd.

“You two are practically wearing a couple’s costume, though. That’s a pretty good start.”

Cipher smirks, patting him on the shoulder. “Should’ve been your tactic,” she says. “But then you would’ve been stealing my genius idea.”

“Unlike someone, I’m not here to get laid,” Mydei rolls his eyes.

“Oh yeah? Why are you here, then?”

Mydei stares at her, unable to mask his obvious irritation. “I don’t know,” he says between his teeth. “Were this evening going my way, I would be asleep right now.”

Cipher cackles, patting his shoulder one more time. “Just keep drinking that nasty shit,” she says. “Who knows, maybe you’ll get lucky and wake up in his bed.”

“Yeah, right. Go away.”

Cipher actually listens, leaving Mydei by himself as he downs his first cup and immediately pours himself another. With each new day that passes, he’s starting to feel less sure about the nature of his relationship with Phainon.

“Are you Kremnoan?”

Mydei nearly jumps out of his skin, having not seen the person who snuck up on him at all. She’s tiny, barely up to his chest, with a mask obscuring most of her face and long brown pigtails. Mydei has never seen her in his life, though that’s probably the case with most of the people here. “Um,” he swallows, holding his cup closer to his chest. “Yes?”

“Hm,” the girl fumbles through her skirts, before procuring a gun prop that looks suspiciously real. “Will you play a game of Belobogian Roulette?”

Mydei takes a tiny step back, hoping his discomfort isn’t as obvious as he feels like it is. “What?” he asks, voice a little unsteady. “Is that real?”

“All you have to do is point this gun at my head and pull the trigger,” she sing-songs, pointing the handle towards him. “And then we both hope it doesn’t fire!”

“I know what Belobogian Roulette is,” he murmurs. “No thank you.”

“Hm,” she says again, thankfully putting the gun down. “Shame.” And then she skips away, whistling.

“What the fuck,” Mydei breathes, finishing off the rest of his punch before going in for a third serving.

“Who was that?” It’s Phainon’s voice, coming up from behind him. “What did she want?”

“For me to shoot her,” Mydei says, voice tired.

“What—”

“Sparkle,” Caelus says, still following Phainon around, apparently. “She’s weird. I don’t know why I invited her.”

“Some people are really into their costumes, I guess,” Phainon shrugs.

“I don’t think it was an act,” Mydei says, at the same time Caelus says it “probably wasn’t an act.” Phainon looks between both of them, confused, then moves between them to serve himself some punch.

“Is this spiked?” he asks, ladle hovering beside his cup.

“Oh, yeah,” Caelus snorts. “Very. Be careful with that shit.”

Mydei is halfway through swallowing down the remnants of his third serving, and slowly lowers the cup down from his mouth. “Fuck,” he mutters, then tosses the cup into a nearby trash can.

“Dude, already? How much did you have?”

“Like three full cups,” Mydei admits. “How bad do you think that is?”

Caelus laughs heartily while Phainon shoots him an extremely concerned glance. “I suggest you start dancing now before you can’t walk anymore,” he says, clapping him on the shoulder. “Unless you’ve built up your tolerance from our college days.”

Mydei hasn’t, not even a little bit. He usually hates getting drunk. He doesn’t know why he’s so eager to tonight. He turns towards the crowd, which starts cheering as a new song comes on. Mydei doesn’t recognize it —he doesn’t exactly spend his time listening to party music.

“Who’s your DJ?” he asks, crossing his arms.

“Forgot her name,” Caelus says, shrugging. “I found her online. She’s popular in Natlan.”

“Huh,” Mydei stares at the crowd, where the rest of the band is dancing together. Cipher looks like she’s having the time of her life, Hyacine is jumping up and down, and Castorice looks extremely uncomfortable.

“Why? Should I request a CALAMITY song?”

“Do that and I’ll kill you,” Mydei says.

“Empty threat,” Phainon chimes in. “Do it. Child’s Play.”

“Why Child’s Play?” Mydei turns to him, frowning. “That song’s not even that good.”

“It’s the only song of yours you can dance to,” Phainon says. “Come on, Mydei.” He throws out his empty cup as Caelus walks away, hopefully not to the DJ booth, and lightly touches Mydei’s arm.

“Should you be dancing?” Mydei asks.

Phainon rolls his eyes. “I can dance, Mydei. Come on.” That makes enough sense to Mydei. He’d been showing off his progress occasionally, how he could bend his fingers enough to pick up a glass or cup now, but he couldn’t quite make a full fist yet. And his finger dexterity had a long way to go. A return to piano was, at the moment, a hope and a dream.

They group up with Cipher and the rest of the band, Hyacine pulling on his hand and yanking his arm up and down as she jumps.

“Come on, pretty boy,” Cipher yells over the loud music. “Kephale didn’t give you that ass for no reason!”

“What?” Mydei yells, looking at her in disbelief. “Don’t say that shit to me ever again!”

“You heard her, Mydei,” Phainon says. His voice isn’t much louder than a murmur, as he speaks right against his ear from behind him.

Mydei whirls around, placing his free hand that Hyacine isn’t holding against the side of his neck. “You’d like to see that, wouldn’t you?”

Phainon’s grin is blinding, and it makes Mydei feel a little lightheaded. Or maybe the overabundance of alcohol he had just had is finally starting to catch up with him. “I think anyone would,” he teases back. There’s a pit in his stomach. He doesn’t know where it came from, or how long it’s been there.

The first chord of Child’s Play rings out around them, and it’s a miracle Mydei doesn’t throw up on Phainon’s shoes right there.

The crowd cheers as the song continues, so loud that Mydei feels frozen in place, unsure what to do with this information. As his voice rings out around them, he can hear what feels like the whole room singing along with him.

“You hear that?” Phainon says, leaning in close as he says it. “You’re famous, Mydeimos.”

“Famous,” Mydei scoffs. “Yeah, right.”

“Little prince!” Cipher yells. “Hold this, would you?” Before he has a chance to process her words, he’s hit in the face with her suit jacket. He lifts his hands, catching it, and glares in her direction, unimpressed. “Be a gentleman,” she adds, with a wink.

“Asshole,” Mydei mutters, folding the jacket over his arm. “Hey, where’s Cas?”

“Getting a drink,” Cipher says. She doesn’t stop moving for a second.

Phainon is distracted by Hyacine, so Mydei uses the opportunity to slip away. He’s never been a very big fan of dancing, anyway.

Castorice, as Cipher said, is pouring herself a cup of punch at the drinks table.

“Careful,” Mydei says, coming up behind her. “Caelus said it’s strong. I had three cups already.”

“How strong?” She asks, dropping the ladle back into the bowl with her cup half full.

“Very? I don’t know.” Mydei rubs at his temples. “I already have a headache.”

“I don’t usually drink, but…” she trails off, cup halfway to her mouth as she stares into the distance. “I’m nervous.”

“Nervous?” Mydei follows her gaze, met with the sight of Cipher, Hyacine, and Phainon dancing together. “Ah.”

Castorice takes a sip, makes a face, and puts her cup down. “You’ve dated many people before, right, Mydei?”

Mydei almost laughs. Were it anyone else, he would think she was calling him a whore. “Three,” he says. “Is that many?”

“By my standards,” she says. “I’m helpless when it comes to these things.”

“That’s okay,” he reassures her. “I’m sure she doesn’t mind.”

“Huh?” Castorice looks at him, flushing through her make up. “Do you know who I’m talking about?”

“Cipher?” He asks. His fingers are starting to feel hot. He tugs at his collar.

“Oh, Kephale,” she mutters. “Am I really so obvious?”

Mydei bites at his bottom lip. “No,” he says, leaning back against the table. “I guessed. I think.”

“I’ve tried so hard to deny it,” Castorice admits. “I don’t want to ruin things. She’s the best friend I’ve ever had. Wouldn’t she think it’s…well, inappropriate of me to harbor such feelings for her?”

“I really don’t think she’d think that,” Mydei says. Despite Cipher’s horrendous attempts at matchmaking between him and Phainon, he doesn’t think it’s his place to comment on Cipher’s feelings for Castorice. She could tell her that herself.

Speaking of Phainon, he can still see him in the crowd. He’s taller than nearly everyone around him. Mydei turns around and starts pouring himself another cup.

“You don’t?” Castorice looks at him, hope flickering in her round eyes.

“No, Cas,” Mydei says. He feels like he’s losing his grip on himself. He tries to blink the weariness out of his eyes, but it doesn’t work. In his haze, he spills the punch all over his hand. “Fuck. Fuck.”

Castorice grabs the ladle out of his hand, putting it back in the bowl. “Are you okay?”

“I am wonderful,” Mydei says, standing awkwardly as he waits for the liquid in his cup to stop spilling over the edge. “Shoot your shot, Cassie. Anyone would be lucky to have you.”

“Oh,” Castorice says softly. She’s a little flushed. “Well. Um, thank you.”

Mydei nods. He presses a hand to his forehead, and feels like the room is spinning as he does. “Fuck,” he mutters.

“Um, are you sure you’re okay?” Castorice asks, carefully placing a hand on his shoulder. Her touch is freezing, and he thinks he flinches.

“Yeah,” he murmurs. “I need to pee.”

He picks a direction and wanders in it, downing his cup as he goes. He tosses it in the closest trash can he can find, and out of the corner of his eye, he can vaguely see Phainon’s unmistakable head of white hair.

He stops walking, uncaring of how he might look as he stares without shame. Phainon is laughing, talking animatedly as he dances with a woman Mydei doesn’t know who has her arm around his neck. He laughs at something she says so loudly that Mydei thinks he can hear it, all the way from where he stands.

He feels sick. He turns, continuing his search for the bathroom. He pushes open a door he thinks must be it, only to find a small sitting room that nearly knocks him out with the smell of marijuana.

“What the fuck,” he hisses, bringing a hand up to his nose.

“Holy shit. No fucking way!” Some girl shouts, jumping up from where she’s seated and running up to him. “Mydei?”

Mydei blinks his eyes open. The woman in front of him is someone he recognizes, though it takes him a second to remember who. Her blonde hair is much longer than it was last time he saw her, but with the same purple streaks running through it. She’s dressed as a rockstar, which is an even bigger giveaway than the purple hair. “Hi, Serval,” he says, flashing her the best grin he can manage.

“Guys, wake up. This is the Mydeimos I’m talking about here,” she says, turning to the rest of the people in the room.

“Can you shut it? I’m locked in right now,” says another girl, sitting on the coffee table with her legs crossed. Mydei isn’t sure what her costume is supposed to be, but she looks like some sort of video game character. She’s holding a video game controller, eyes glued to the TV screen. Mydei has no idea what she’s playing, but it looks like some kind of first person shooter.

There’s another girl with a long white wig knocked out in the corner. Mydei doesn’t know her, but he thinks she’s also supposed to be a vampire.

“What’s up, Dei,” Stelle sits sprawled out across the couch cushions wearing what seems to be a felt trash can, with a smile on her face that never seems to fade. Her eyes are so bloodshot that Mydei has no choice but to assume most of the weed smell in the room is her doing.

“Don’t call me that,” he says, collapsing back against the door. “Did you smoke all of that shit?”

“Are you asking for some?” Serval says, going back to her seat on the other empty couch.

Mydei rubs at his temples. He knows it’s a bad idea, and he hates how long he considers it. He’s not quite past the point of no return just yet, but he knows that’s where he’s headed. “No,” he decides, as the last part of his good judgment fades. “Do you have any alcohol?”

“Sure,” Serval says, pulling a bottle and two shot glasses out of a plastic bag. It looks like incredibly cheap alcohol. Mydei doesn’t want to know who in this room bought it, or where they bought it from. That’s not information he needs right now. “That’s Acheron, by the way.” Serval says, as she uncaps the bottle and fills both glasses. “You should check out her music. She’s also a classical musician turned rockstar.”

“Acheron? Like the river?”

“Um…maybe?”

“FUCK,” the girl on the table yells, loudly enough to burst Mydei’s eardrums. She continues to yell at the TV, currently displaying a “deceased” screen, using more creative profanities than Mydei has ever heard in his life. Clearly he hasn’t been cursing to his full potential.

“Dude, chill the fuck out,” Stelle groans, grabbing a throw pillow and tossing it over her eyes.

“Why don’t you introduce yourself to our guest,” Serval suggests, handing him his shot glass. He takes it, clinks it against Serval’s own, and tries not to wince as they take them together. It’s been a long time since he’s taken a shot. It’s so much worse than he remembers.

“Silver Wolf,” the girl says, watching him over her shoulder.

Mydei blinks, unable to focus very hard on anything other than the taste in his mouth. “…Huh?”

She rolls her eyes. “My name, obviously.”

Mydei’s head is pounding. He puts the shot glass down on the table and puts all his energy into deciphering what this girl is trying to tell him. “… What?”

“Oh my god,” she mutters, turning back to her video game and selecting the respawn option.

“Her name is Silver Wolf,” Serval explains.

Mydei crashes against the cough cushions behind him. “Your name is Silver Wolf,” he confirms, to which she seems to nod very slowly. “What the fuck kind of parents did you have?”

Stelle giggles at that, vaguely reminding Mydei of her existence, as he begins to cough his lungs out at another fruitless attempt to get the alcohol taste out of his mouth.

Serval tosses him a plastic water bottle, which lands in his lap when he’s unable to process it fast enough. “Water,” she says, like that wasn’t obvious.

Mydei nods, taking a big swig of water. It’s cold going down his throat, and brings him more relief than he’d like to admit.

He can’t get the image of Phainon out of his head. He wants another shot.

“How drunk are you?” Serval asks, following his request.

Mydei shrugs. “Not enough.”

Serval sighs, reaching for the bottle to pour him another one. “I get it, man,” she murmurs. “The world is going to shit, y’know?”

The second one doesn’t go down any easier, but he has some water this time, which helps. “Cipher was right,” he admits, closing his eyes and falling onto his side. “I’m in love with him.”

Stelle giggles again, the sound muffled by the pillow over her face. “Yay,” she says, dragging out the word. “Young love.”

Mydei groans, rolling onto his stomach. Half his body is off the couch, the rest of him slowly sliding down until he falls onto the floor in a heap. “Ow,” he complains, rubbing his head.

“Mydei,” Serval says, and Mydei can faintly hear her stand up before she comes to kneel in front of him. “Are you okay?”

“No, no…” Mydei drawls, words slurring together. “No…”

“You’re wasted,” Serval decides. She tries to pull him to a sitting position, but it’s fruitless. “Seriously, Mydei, how much did you drink before this?”

“Not much,” Mydei presses his forehead into the carpet.

“Mydei, can you sit up? You need to drink some more water.”

Mydei pulls himself upright with much effort, reaching above him for the water bottle she had just given him. He can’t find it, until Serval gets up and hands it to him. “I need to pee,” he decides, stumbling a little as he gets to his feet instead.

“Okay,” Serval says, nodding. She guides him to the door, opening it and pointing across the room. “Over there. Make sure you drink the water, yeah?”

“Yeah, yeah,” Mydei says, waving her off. “Thanks, Serval…I love you.”

“Love you too, man. Come back here when you’re done, alright?”

Mydei can’t hear her that well, distracted by the earsplitting music once again. He doesn’t think the song they’re playing now is as bad as it was before, so he heads back towards the dance floor, Serval’s words and his original goal of going to the bathroom quickly forgotten.

Phainon is nowhere to be seen. Mydei moves through the crowd, knocked around by bodies hitting him as he stands in place, mesmerized by the flashing lights with nothing in his head but the sound of the music.

“Mydei!” He’s tugged in one direction, some girl’s hand on his wrist. He blinks, trying to make out who it is, and sees Cipher’s unmistakable gray hair and suit. She’s missing her jacket. Mydei vaguely remembers her giving it to him, but has no idea where he put it. “Having fun?” she asks, winking.

Mydei can’t form words. He doesn’t know if she’s twirling him around, or if the room is spinning on its own. He thinks it might be the latter.

“Where’s Phainon?” he asks. He squeezes his eyes shut like it might stop the room from collapsing around him.

“Over there,” Cipher says, pointing in another direction. “Last I saw him, anyway. Better hurry up, he’s a hot commodity tonight!”

Mydei tugs his arm away with as much force as he can muster, moving through the crowd to where she said Phainon was. He thinks he can hear someone call his name, but ignores it with one clear goal in mind.

Finally, he spots him—that head of white hair, bouncing up and down in the crowd. He’s taller than most people around him, even a little taller than Mydei himself.

“Phainon,” he murmurs, making his way toward him. “There you are.” He practically throws himself in the man’s arms, who doesn’t stop dancing for a second.

“Woah, hey there,” Phainon says, placing both his hands on Mydei’s shoulders. “How’d I get so lucky tonight?”

“Lucky?” Mydei asks, frowning. “You’re not lucky. I only want you.”

“Yeah?” Phainon whispers against Mydei’s ear. “How bad?”

Mydei pulls away. His eyes are so bright, almost blinding, so he looks down at his lips instead. They’re slightly parted, the most beautiful shade of red, even through the flashing lights. Mydei wants to kiss him so badly it hurts.

So he does, leaning in until there’s no room left. The feeling of Phainon’s lips on his sends tingles through his entire body. He feels like he could be floating as he presses his hips flush into Phainon’s body, like they can’t get close enough.

Phainon is greedy, licking into Mydei’s mouth with the same sort of urgency. One of his hands trails down Mydei’s back, pawing at his ass through the fabric of his pants.

Mydei pulls away, panting. “Bathroom,” he manages, then grabs his wrist and pulls him away.

He bumps into no less than ten people, on his way out of the crowd, and his hip slams against the drink table. Phainon catches him, one hand on his back. “You okay?”

“Yeah,” Mydei whispers. “Never better.”

He pushes Phainon against the bathroom door the second they’re inside. He thinks it’s empty, and his fingers trip over each other as he locks it. He can’t see straight. He can’t feel his tongue. He thinks he’s started to see the world in 8-bit.

There are no more clear thoughts in his head as he sinks to his knees. He fumbles with the belt buckle before him for so long, he’s not sure how it actually comes loose.

The last clear thing he can remember is the feeling of strong hands grabbing fistfuls of his hair.
